claim: Roannais hosts five officially labeled Villages de Caractère en Loire: Saint-Haon-le-Châtel, Saint-Jean-Saint-Maurice-sur-Loire, Ambierle, Perreux and Le Crozet.
quote: Saint-Haon-le-Châtel is one of the five villages labeled 'Village of Character in the Loire' of Roannais, alongside Saint-Jean-Saint-Maurice-sur-Loire, Ambierle, Perreux and Le Crozet.

claim: The Benedictine Abbey of Charlieu, founded c.875 and attached to Cluny in the 10th century, sits about 25 minutes north of Roanne and is Charlieu's main anchor sight.
quote: Benedictine Abbey in Charlieu, 25 minutes from Roanne ... Founded around 875, the Benedictine abbey of Charlieu was attached in the middle of the 10th century to the great Burgundian abbey of Cluny.

claim: Charlieu Benedictine Abbey admission is 5€ full, 4€ reduced, free under 12; a guided tour adds 3€.
quote: Full price: €5. Reduced rate: €4 (ages 12-18, students, job seekers, disabled persons). Free entry for children under 12 ... Guided tours supplement: €3 additional.

claim: Charlieu's outdoor market runs Wednesday and Saturday mornings on Boulevard Jacquard, a tradition dating back to a 1207 charter.
quote: The market is held on Wednesday mornings on Boulevard Jacquard ... On Saturday mornings, there is also a market ... a market had already been taking place each Wednesday and Saturday since 1207.

claim: The Cordeliers Convent in Saint-Nizier-sous-Charlieu has one of the few preserved medieval Franciscan cloisters in France, with a Rayonnant Gothic north gallery whose capitals depict vices and virtues.
quote: The cloister of the Cordeliers convent is one of the few medieval Franciscan cloisters still preserved in France ... in the Rayonnant Gothic style, ... north gallery adorned with figurative capitals humorously depicting vices and virtues.

claim: Ambierle Priory, 18 km from Roanne, houses a 5-meter Flemish altarpiece (1466) with paintings attributed to Rogier van der Weyden and a sculpted Passion of Christ.
quote: located north of the Loire department, 18 km from Roanne ... An altarpiece dated 1466 ... paintings attributed to the great Flemish painter Rogier van der Weyden ... polyptych, which extends over 5 meters.

claim: Saint-Haon-le-Châtel, 14th-century capital of Roannais, retains a moated enclosure with 18 towers and four gates — the only Loire commune to preserve this medieval configuration — plus a medieval garden and Romanesque church.
quote: the only commune in Loire to have retained this medieval configuration. The fortifications feature a moated enclosure with eighteen towers and four gates ... medieval garden featuring more than one hundred plants ... Romanesque church with magnificent restored medieval wall paintings.

claim: Le Crozet, one of Roanne's four medieval strongholds, holds a 12th-century dungeon, 13th-century Maison de Bois, the listed Grande Porte and a Museum of Popular Arts and Traditions in a 16th-century turreted house.
quote: houses from the 13th, 15th and 16th centuries ... the great gate (a listed Historical Monument), the Maison de Bois (Wooden House) from the 13th century ... Dungeon from the 12th century ... Museum of Popular Arts and Traditions in a 15th century house with a corner turret.

claim: La Pacaudière, ~25 minutes from Roanne, preserves the Grande Porte of a fortified enclosure, half-timbered Maison du Connétable, arcaded Halle de la Cordouannerie and the Petit Louvre, a Gothic-Renaissance hybrid listed since 1932.
quote: La Pacaudière has 1000 inhabitants and is located 25 minutes from Roanne ... pass under the Grande Porte ... Maison du Connétable with half-timbered walls ... The iconic Petit Louvre, a building from the early 16th century classified as a historic monument since July 1932.

claim: Priory of Pommiers-en-Forez, ~30 minutes from Roanne, has four massive towers, was preserved through the Revolution, has been Loire-département-owned since 1990, and is accessible only by guided tour.
quote: Priory of Pommiers in Pommiers-en-Forez, 30 minutes from Roanne ... With its four massive towers ... preserved by its successive owners until the site was acquired by the Loire department in 1990 ... accessible to the public, only by guided tour.

claim: Saint-Jean-Saint-Maurice-sur-Loire perches over the Loire on the Cluny/Le Puy pilgrimage route; the 17 m Tour de Saint-Maurice keep gives a 360° view over the Villerest dam, and artisan workshops (pottery, foundry) plus a Sunday summer market enliven the village July–August.
quote: The keep called Tour de Saint-Maurice ... dominates the village from its 17 meters and offers a 360° panorama over the waters of the dam ... Every Sunday morning between July and August, the village offers a summer market.

claim: Perreux became the 5th Roannais Village de Caractère in 2022; sights include a remnant castle tower, an 11th-century chapel, fortified gate, two flamboyant Gothic chapels and around 15 half-timbered houses from the 15th–16th centuries.
quote: Perreux became, in 2022, the 5e Village of Character in Roannais ... There remains of the castle the tower, a chapel of the XIe century and the old fortified gate ... two chapels in flamboyant Gothic style ... Around fifteen half-timbered houses date from the 15th and 16th century.

claim: Domaine Sérol in Renaison offers free tastings without appointment Monday-Saturday 9am-12pm and 2pm-7pm, closed Sundays and holidays.
quote: Tastings are complimentary for individuals and small groups, no appointment necessary. Monday to Saturday from 9:00 am to 12:00 pm and from 2:00 pm to 7:00 pm

claim: Domaine Sérol produces biodynamic Gamay Saint Romain reds on the Côte Roannaise with views over the Roanne plain.
quote: Domaine Sérol produces biodynamic wines on the Côte Roannaise, mainly red wines from the local grape variety Gamay Saint Romain

claim: Domaine des Pothiers in Villemontais opens weekdays 9am-12pm and 1pm-5pm, with Saturday visits by appointment only; tastings €5 for groups.
quote: Opening hours are Monday through Friday between 9 am and 12 pm and between 1 pm and 5 pm, closed on Sundays. Saturday visits are by appointment, with a maximum group size of 15 people.

claim: Domaine des Pothiers is a 21-hectare estate in the southernmost Côte Roannaise producing Gamay, Chardonnay, and Pinot Gris wines plus an ancestral-method sparkling rosé.
quote: the estate is 21Ha (52 acres) wide... white wine from the Pinot Gris grape variety, red wine vinified and aged in barrels, an ancestral method rosé sparkling wine

claim: Domaine de la Rochette (Néron family) in Villemontais farms 16 hectares of organic Gamay, Chardonnay, and Pinot Gris on granite soil, with 45-minute cellar visits plus tasting by appointment at €5pp including farmhouse cheeses.
quote: The domain has 16 hectares of vines planted with Gamay (St Romain), Chardonnay, and Pinot Gris varieties that are cultivated on granite soil... Visits consist of two parts: visiting the cellars followed by tasting, lasting approximately 45 minutes, by appointment. The cost is 5 € per person

claim: Domaine de la Bénisson-Dieu in Ambierle sits on the northern edge of the AOC with 2.6 hectares farmed organically and using natural winemaking.
quote: Domaine de La Bénisson-Dieu is located on the northern edge of the Côte Roannaise AOC with 2.6 hectares in production, and is organic with natural winemaking

claim: Summer 'Apéros de la Côte' winegrower encounters (June-September, ~15 domaines) run roughly 1h30 for €18 per person including a 4-wine tasting and local products.
quote: about fifteen winegrowers welcome visitors to discover their domains and wines, with encounters lasting approximately 1h30 and concluding with wine tasting and regional specialties. The visits cost €18 per person

claim: Les Halles Diderot covered market runs Tuesday-Sunday 8am-7pm (Sunday until noon); Roanne also has open-air markets on Tuesday and Friday at Place du Marché, Friday at Place de l'Hôtel de Ville, and Sunday at Place Georges Clemenceau, all 8am-1pm.
quote: Marché des Halles Diderot – mardi, mercredi, jeudi, vendredi, samedi, dimanche de 8h à 19h... Place du marché – mardi, vendredi de 8h à 13h... Place de l'Hôtel de Ville – Friday, 8am-1pm

claim: Mons Fromager-Affineur (the renowned cheesemonger Hervé Mons) has a stall at Les Halles Diderot in Roanne open Tuesday-Sunday, Friday/Saturday 8am-12:30pm and 3-7:30pm.
quote: Tuesday to Thursday: 8:00 AM to 12:30 PM and 3:00 PM to 7:00 PM; Friday and Saturday: 8:00 AM to 12:30 PM and 3:00 PM to 7:30 PM; Sunday: 9:00 AM to 12:00 PM

claim: Maison Mons, based in Saint-Haon-le-Châtel, ages cheeses in a rehabilitated 180-meter former railway tunnel at Ambierle.
quote: A former railway tunnel located in Ambierle, 180 meters long, was rehabilitated into exceptional maturing cellars

claim: Maison Pralus, founded in Roanne in 1948 by Auguste Pralus, created the iconic Praluline brioche with pink pralines in 1955 and now operates as a bean-to-bar chocolatier.
quote: Maison Pralus was founded in 1948 by Auguste Pralus... Praluline®, a brioche with homemade pink pralines created in 1955. François Pralus expanded the chocolate business, becoming one of the few artisans producing chocolate from bean to bar

claim: Pralus operates a flagship boutique inside Les Halles Diderot in Roanne, plus a second Roanne shop on Charles de Gaulle and an additional boutique in Renaison.
quote: Pralus Roanne pastry and chocolate shop, Les Halles Diderot

claim: Saint-Haon-le-Châtel is a fortified medieval village perched above the Roanne plain, one of five 'Village de Caractère en Loire' in the Roannais and a worthwhile detour combined with cellar visits.
quote: Saint-Haon-le-Châtel est l'un des cinq villages labellisés 'Village de Caractère en Loire' du Roannais

claim: Abbaye de Charlieu admission is €5 full / €4 reduced with under-12 free, and a 4-site 'Explorez la Loire au fil des siècles' pass costs €12 covering the Couvent des Cordeliers and other departmental sites.
quote: Plein tarif : 5 € … Tarif réduit : 4 € … Gratuité : enfants de moins de 12 ans … Le pass annuel 'Explorez la Loire au fil des siècles' … Entrées illimitées pour les 4 sites

claim: Charlieu Abbey is open Monday and Wednesday–Sunday 10am–1pm and 2–6pm April–October (closed Tuesdays and 1 May), shorter 2–5pm afternoons February–March and November–December, and shut for January.
quote: April-October: Monday, Wednesday-Friday, weekends 10am-1pm, 2-6pm (closed May 1st) … February-March: Monday, Wednesday-Friday, weekends 10am-1pm, 2-5pm

claim: The Couvent des Cordeliers at Saint-Nizier-sous-Charlieu, just across the Sornin from the abbey, charges €5 full / €4 reduced (€8 with guided tour) at 1 Chemin des Cordeliers, 42190.
quote: Standard admission: €5 … Reduced rate: €4 … Admission with guided/thematic tour: €8 standard, €7 reduced … 1 Chemin des Cordeliers, 42190 Saint Nizier sous Charlieu

claim: The convent preserves one of the rare medieval Franciscan cloisters surviving in France, a Rayonnant Gothic ensemble whose north gallery is lined with figurative capitals.
quote: The cloister of the Cordeliers convent is one of the few medieval Franciscan cloisters still preserved in France. The grand cloister, in Rayonnant Gothic style, has very refined decoration, and its north gallery in particular is adorned with figurative capitals.

claim: The priory's centrepiece is the 5.60-metre Passion altarpiece, a Brussels polyptych of c. 1466 attributed to the workshop of Rogier van der Weyden or his successor, commissioned by Michel de Chaugy.
quote: This polyptych, which extends over 5.60m, comprises a central sculpted section retracing the Passion of Christ and shutters … The work bears a Brussels mark; various historical clues thus designate Brabant as the place of creation, around 1466, and probably the workshop of Roger Van der Weyden or his successor.

claim: Musée Alice Taverne in Ambierle, set in an 18th-c bourgeois house, recreates Roannais–Forez rural life 1850–1940 with workshops, a village dressmaker, country inn and 1940s daily-life rooms.
quote: The permanent exhibitions showcase rural life from the 1850s through WWII, featuring: Domestic scenes of peasant women … Village tradespeople's workshops, including a clockmaker and barrel maker … A recreated village dressmaker's shop and country inn

claim: Château de la Roche perches at 437 m on a rocky pinnacle above the Loire gorges at Saint-Priest-la-Roche, staging five 'show rooms' with theatrical scenography and seasonal escape games.
quote: Perched at 437 meters elevation … sits on 'a rocky peak since the 13th century' and 'overhangs the river' … 'five show rooms' that chronicle different historical periods through theatrical scenography

claim: Entry costs €8 full / €6 reduced with under-6s free; the castle runs daily in summer (9.30–12.30 and 14–19 from 6 July to 31 August 2026) and weekends-plus in shoulder months, closing in winter.
quote: From July 6 to August 31, 2026, it's open daily from 9:30 am to 12:30 pm and from 2 pm to 7 pm … Full price is €8, reduced price is €6 … free entry for children under 6

claim: The Musée Joseph Déchelette at 22 rue Anatole France in Roanne charges €5 full / €2.80 reduced with under-26s free, and offers free entry every Wednesday afternoon and on the first Sunday of each month.
quote: Full price: 5 € … Reduced rate: 2.80 € … Free for under 26s … Access to permanent collections is free on Wednesday afternoons and free for everyone on the first Sunday of each month.

claim: Housed in an 18th-c hôtel particulier with its garden, the Déchelette museum spans Prehistory to the 20th century with strong holdings in archaeology, Egyptian and East-Asian art, photography and one of France's richest provincial ceramics collections including 700 pieces of revolutionary earthenware.
quote: rich and varied course from Prehistory to the 20th century, open to extra-Western arts (Japan, China, Africa), Egyptian art, photography … one of the richest provincial ceramic collections (700 pieces of revolutionary earthenware, Sèvres porcelain, etc.)

claim: Château de Boisy in Pouilly-les-Nonains, just west of Roanne, is a 15th-c fortified manor bought in 1447 by royal treasurer Jacques Cœur; its square donjon and round towers are listed historic monuments (inscrit 1927, classé 1931).
quote: Jacques Cœur acquired it in 1447 … features a square donjon (keep) and round towers … inscription in 1927 for facades and roofs, classification in 1931 for exterior sections of south and east wings, southeast round tower and northeast square donjon

claim: The Villerest Un sightseeing boat operates April 1–October 31 with a 1h cruise to St-Jean-St-Maurice at 3pm daily except Wed/Sun, and from May to end of August a 3h30 cruise to Château de la Roche at 9am on Wed/Sun, all by reservation.
quote: From April 1 to October 31, there is a 1 hour walk to St-Jean-St-Maurice-sur-Loire, with departure at 3 p.m. every day except Wednesdays and Sundays. From May to the end of August on Wednesdays and Sundays: 3h30 walk to the Château de la Roche at 9 a.m. All walks are by reservation.

claim: The Roanne-Iguerande section of the Véloire greenway is 24 km of fully paved cycle path with minimal elevation (259–276m), rated suitable for all cyclists and family-friendly with picnic tables along the route.
quote: Length: 24 km. Surface: Entirely smooth cycle path (100%). Elevation: Minimal - 11m ascents, 0m descents; ranges from 259m to 276m. Difficulty: Suitable for all cyclists... 'a stage suitable for all cyclists' with 'many picnic tables and loungers'

claim: The Roanne-Digoin canal is 56 km long with ten locks, and the towpath hosts a 25 km greenway from the Port of Roanne to Charlieu via Briennon — marked, accessible for reduced mobility, and electric bikes are rentable at the harbour master's office.
quote: The canal is 56 kilometres long and has ten locks... 25 secure and marked kilometers await cyclists, hikers and Sunday strollers... This greenway also allows people with reduced mobility, rollerblading or running enthusiasts... Electric bike rentals are available at the harbor master's office

claim: Côte Roannaise day-hike options include the easy 9 km Monts de la Madeleine loop from Villemontais (+349m) and the 4–7 km easy-to-moderate Gorge du Désert circuit from Saint-Alban-les-Eaux, plus a 17.9 km easy Moulins Chérier loop.
quote: Grande boucle des Moulins Chérier | 17.92 km | +517 m | Easy (Cherier). Les Monts de la Madeleine (Villemontais) | 9.04 km | +349 m | Easy. Gorge du Désert | 4.37–6.96 km | +194–360 m | Easy–Moderate (Saint-Alban-les-Eaux)

claim: The Côte Roannaise vineyard spans about 215 hectares on a 20 km terraced hillside, AOC since 1994, with around thirty winegrowers across roughly ten villages including Renaison and Saint-Haon-le-Châtel.
quote: The Côte Roannaise vineyard radiates over a 20-kilometer-long, terraced hillside, and the 215 hectares of the Côte Roannaise vineyard are located in the north of the Loire department and are recognized as an AOC since 1994, with around thirty winegrowers on more than 200 hectares and around ten villages.

claim: The Côte Roannaise wine route runs about 55 km from La Pacaudière in the north to Saint-Jean-Saint-Maurice-sur-Loire, crossing 12 appellation communes and doable as a one-day scenic drive.
quote: The wine route stretches from La Pacaudière in the north to Saint-Jean-Saint-Maurice-sur-Loire, south of Roanne, a distance of approximately 55 km, and this route crosses 12 communes within the appellation. You can explore this exceptional itinerary, combining nature, heritage, and gastronomy, in one day.

claim: The free Belvédère de Commelle-Vernay site offers views over the dam, a two-metre two-sided sundial, an orientation table, and a picnic area, and serves as the boarding station for the Loire tourist activity.
quote: The site offers magnificent views of the dam, the village of Villerest, the church and the Vernay bridge. On this site there is a gigantic two-sided sundial, a vertical disc two meters in diameter... The site features an orientation table, the Loire tourist train station, and a picnic area.

claim: Belvédère Aventures in Commelle-Vernay (10 min from Roanne) replaces the old tourist train with electric-assist 4-seater railbikes covering a 6.8 km round-trip in 1h30, with 2026 departures from 4 April at 10:00, 11:30, 14:00, 15:30; reservation mandatory.
quote: Situated in Commelle-Vernay, approximately 10 minutes from Roanne... 6,8 km A/R s'effectue en 1H30 en mode balade... For the 2026 season starting April 4th, departures occur at 10:00, 11:30, 14:00, and 15:30... LA RESERVATION EST INDISPENSABLE!

claim: Roanne in late May/early June averages highs around 23°C with lows around 12°C, ~15.7 hours of daylight in June, ~33% chance of rain on a given June day — generally good for hiking, cycling and boating.
quote: the weather in Roanne in June is mildly cool and breezy, with average highs of 74°F (23°C) and lows of 53°F (12°C)... In Roanne in June, there's a 33% chance of rain on an average day... The average day in Roanne during June has 15.7 hours of daylight

claim: Port de la Caille at Saint-Jean-Saint-Maurice-sur-Loire is a pleasure port on the Villerest dam with sailing, fishing and water-launching services, open seasonally 15 March – 30 October.
quote: The Port de la Caille is a pleasure port on the Villerest Dam, located in Saint-Jean-Saint-Maurice-sur-Loire... welcomes water sports, fishing and sailing enthusiasts with warmth and conviviality for a season from March 15 to October 30.

claim: Driving from Ouches to Charlieu is 25-26 km and takes 29-34 minutes.
quote: 25,0 km à 26,0 km ... 29 min à 34 min

claim: Driving from Ouches to Ambierle is 14.7-16.0 km and takes 14-17 minutes.
quote: 14,7 km à 16,0 km ... 14 min à 17 min

claim: Driving from Ouches to Saint-Haon-le-Châtel is 9.7-10.9 km and takes 11-13 minutes.
quote: 9,7 km à 10,9 km ... 11 min à 13 min

claim: Driving from Ouches to Le Crozet is 23.0-24.1 km and takes 21-26 minutes.
quote: 23,0 km à 24,1 km ... 21 min à 26 min

claim: Driving from Ouches to Saint-Priest-la-Roche (Château de la Roche) is 18.9-19.2 km and takes 24-26 minutes.
quote: 18,9 km à 19,2 km ... 24 min à 26 min

claim: Driving from Ouches to Pommiers-en-Forez is 26.7-28.6 km and takes 21-24 minutes.
quote: 26,7 km à 28,6 km ... 21 min à 24 min

claim: Driving from Ouches to Villerest (lake) is 5.2 km and takes 7 minutes.
quote: 5,2 km ... 7 min

claim: Driving from Ouches to Saint-Étienne-le-Molard (Bâtie d'Urfé) is 38.4-40.3 km and takes 31-36 minutes — just outside the 30 km radius.
quote: 38,4 km à 40,3 km ... 31 min à 36 min

claim: Château de la Roche is open Wednesday-Friday and weekends 10:00-12:30 and 14:00-18:30 from 4 April to 3 July 2026, including Sundays; exceptionally open on May 25 (Whit Monday).
quote: From April 4 to July 3, 2026, the castle is open on Wednesday, Thursday, Friday and weekends between 10 am and 12:30 pm and between 2 pm and 6:30 pm. It is open exceptionally on May 1, 8, 14 and 25.

claim: Prieuré de Pommiers is open weekends (incl. Sundays) and Monday/Wednesday/Thursday/Friday from 1 April to 31 October 2026, closed Tuesdays.
quote: Du 1er avril au 31 octobre 2026 : le lundi, mercredi, jeudi, vendredi, jours fériés et les week-ends

claim: Château de la Bâtie d'Urfé is open Mon/Wed/Thu/Fri and weekends 10:00-13:00 and 14:00-18:00 from 1 April to 31 October, closed Tuesdays.
quote: From April 1 to October 31, the château is open Monday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday and weekends between 10 am and 1 pm and between 2 pm and 6 pm.

claim: In May 2026 France observes Victoire 1945 (Fri 8 May), Ascension (Thu 14 May), and Whit Monday/Lundi de Pentecôte (Mon 25 May); no public holidays in June 2026.
quote: Lundi de Pentecôte (Whit Monday) is Monday, May 25, 2026 ... No official public holidays fall in June 2026 in mainland France.

claim: On Sunday 31 May 2026, the opening concert of the Festival des Monts de la Madeleine takes place at the church of Renaison (5pm, ensemble vocal Ô); the 'Chant de l'Aix' festival runs 29-31 May at Saint-Germain-Laval; helicopter flights over the Loire gorges and Lac de Villerest are available.
quote: Concert d'ouverture du Festival des Monts de la Madeleine ... Église de Renaison ... La 3ème édition du festival 'Chant de l'Aix' se déroulera du 29 au 31 mai à Baffy, Saint-Germain Laval

claim: Charlieu's Grande Fête Médiévale 'Les Portes du Temps' falls on 24-26 July 2026 — not in late May, so unavailable for this weekend.
quote: Grande Fête médiévale, Les Portes du Temps - 25 au 27 juillet

claim: Charlieu's food market days are Wednesday and Saturday mornings (8am-1pm) — not Sunday.
quote: the food market takes place year-round on Wednesdays and Saturdays from 8am to 1pm at Boulevard Jacquard

claim: Roanne in late May/early June averages highs of 19-22°C with May being the wettest month (97 mm rainfall) and June drier (58 mm); ~7 hours of daily sunshine.
quote: May is the wettest month in Roanne with 97 mm of rainfall. June receives approximately 58 mm of precipitation ... May is significantly sunnier with 7 hours of sunshine per day
